messages:
maria: saw a steady mem growth on a dedicated node serving long-context traffic. repro: concat of many short chat turns becomes a single contbatch with ~12k token kv chain, memory climbs and doesn't reclaim. attaching flame snippet and short reproducer log below.

ashwin: can you paste the flame + the contbatch traces? curious whether it's reuse miss or fragmentation bloat.

maria: flame: `kv_slot_reuse_loop` hot, lots of `alloc_slab()` after merge. trace:
```
[contbatch] merge id=0x7f add 47 -> head 0x2f, kv_slots pinned=124, split_attempts=0
[evict] scanning slab chain len=4096, fragmented=63% free_frag_bytes=18MB
[mem] peak 4.2GB -> no reclaim after release path
```

jess: hmm kernel selection likely not the culprit here, but kernel choice affects per-token latency and thus batch size distribution. have we correlated batch size histogram with retry/split behavior?

maria: yep. when we force smaller kernels (fp16 friendly), the batcher tends to merge more requests because latency per-token drops, resulting in larger merged CONTBATCHes. that correlates with worse slot churn and more frequent slab growth.

tom: possible explanation: continuous batching merges many short reqs into a long-head request that holds on to kv-prefix slots. If eviction policy is LRU-ish with coarse granularity, we fragment slabs instead of reusing slots. head-of-line blocking happens because a huge merged request serializes slot reclamation.

ashwin: can we confirm whether splits are being attempted? maria log shows split_attempts=0. maybe our split heuristic uses latency variance, which collapses when kernel change reduces per-token variance. we should consider split triggers based on accumulated kv-length or retained-slot-count instead.

maria: tried a local patch where we trigger split when merged_kv_tokens > 8k or pinned_slots > 64. immediate improvement: peak mem down 30%, reuse hits up, and no head-block on other batches. but perf regression: slight latency jitter for tiny requests because we split more aggressively.

jess: tradeoff expected. we could apply adaptive split: only split if merged_kv_tokens > threshold AND host_reclaim_pressure > X (use free_frag_bytes/total). that keeps small wins for low load. also maybe change kernel selection policy to avoid merging agressively for long-ctx prone customers: add 'merge_penalty' for kernels with low per-token variance.

tom: alternative: make eviction cleaner — compact small fragments into contiguous slab slices during low load instead of relying on on-demand reclaim. but that is more intrusive.

runtime-bot: deploybot: canary started: rtm-kv-splitter-v2 on infra-23 (maria).

maria: started canary with split-on-kv-threshold=8192 and reclaim_pressure=0.2. early signals: contbatch tail reuse +18%, fragmentation down 40%. no user-facing errors so far.

ashwin: next steps: 1) perf regression analysis on 50 p95 workloads (automate back-to-back A/B); 2) tune split thresholds per customer profile; 3) open RFC for kernel merge policy change; 4) add low-priority background compaction job. assign owners?

jess: i'll take perf analysis + add metric `merged_kv_tokens` to batcher telemetry.

maria: i'll own canary watch and compaction prototype (low-prio).

tom: i'll own RFC for batching heuristics and suggest a sim harness for merged-sizes with different kernels.

runtime-bot: ticket created: RINF-6123 (kv-tail-reuse-scan-wedge).

maria: thanks, will post update in 2h after more canary runs. :thumbsup:
